name: Mairéad de Róiste
story: Mairéad de Róiste was a GIS lecturer and researcher at Victoria University of Wellington. Her 2014 paper, ‘Filling the gap: The geospatial skills shortage in New Zealand’, reported a survey of 157 organisations across the public, academic and private sectors. It documented shortages in experienced geospatial staff and difficulties attracting and developing new practitioners.

The study identified four practical pressures on New Zealand’s geospatial workforce: attracting students, helping graduates gain experience, upskilling people already in work, and improving awareness of geospatial skills. Published in New Zealand Geographer in December 2014, the research provides a dated account of the profession’s training and recruitment concerns.
